FORM NO. 3

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............

C.S.C, Special Branch Station
REPORT
Date September 18th 38.

Subject (in full) Observation duty aboard the s.s. "Empress of Japan" on
arrival of the late Mr. Singloh Hsu.

Made by D.S. Hocking Forwarded by Inspector E. Talty

The undersigned, accompanied by C.D.S.156 and
C.D.C.s 107 and 357, met the s.s. "Empress of Japan" at the
Hongkew and Shanghai Wharf when the vessel docked at 8 a.m.
on September 18, 1938. Observation was carried out in
No.4 hold over the coffin containing the body of the late
Mr. Singloh Hsu until 8.40 a.m. when the coffin was taken
over by Mr. Horton of the International Funeral Directors
and transferred to the tender "Victoria". Two foreign
members of the River Police were in attendance on the trip
to the Customs Jetty where a Municipal Police escort under
S.I. Fernandez awaited the tender's arrival at 9 a.m.
No untoward incident took place.

D.S. Hocking
D. S.

D.C.(Special Branch).

报告
日期：1938年9月18日。

事由（全称）：在已故徐新六先生抵达时，于“日本皇后”号轮船上执行观察任务。

制作人：D.S. Hocking    转呈人：督察 E. Talty

具报人会同 C.D.S.156 及 C.D.C.s 107 和 357，于1938年9月18日上午8时“日本皇后”号轮船在虹口与上海码头靠岸时前往迎接。观察工作在第4号货舱内进行，直至上午8时40分，装有已故徐新六先生遗体的棺木由国际殡仪馆的霍顿（Horton）先生接管，并转移至驳船“维多利亚”号。两名外籍水上警察成员随行护送前往海关码头，一支由警佐费尔南德斯（Fernandez）率领的工部局警察护卫队于上午9时在码头等候驳船抵达。期间未发生任何意外事件。

D.S. Hocking
侦探警佐

侦探长（特别分部）。

Singloh Hsu's

The body of Mr. Singloh Hsu,
late Shanghai banker, is arriving
in Shanghai this morning on
the Empress of Japan, which is
due here at about 6 o'clock.
Members of Mr. Hsu's family,
who are now in Shanghai, have
arranged for transferring the
coffin from the ship to a lighter
as soon as the Empress boat
docks.
Information regarding plans
for Mr. Hsu's funeral was not
available last night. A private
memorial meeting was held here
by members of Mr. Hsu's family
and his close friends sometime
ago.

《字林西报》。

1938年9月18日

徐新六遗体
预计今日抵沪

已故上海银行家徐新六先生的遗体将于今晨乘“日本皇后”号抵达上海，该轮预计约在6点钟到达。目前在沪的徐先生家属已安排在该轮靠岸后，立即将棺木从船上转移至驳船。
昨晚尚未获悉关于徐先生葬礼计划的详情。此前，徐先生的家属及其密友曾在沪举行过一次私人追悼会。

Morning Post publishes what
purports to be a translation of
an extract from the Hongkong
Nippo of August 24, which, in
view of denials from Tokyo,
makes interesting reading.
The Nippo's headlines are

“Sun Fo Escapes. Surprise

The extract itself states,
among other things, that “it

香港，《日本日报》
称飞机遭袭
旨在捕获孙科

（路透社）
伦敦，8月30日—今日的《晨邮报》刊登了一篇据称是翻译自8月24日香港《日本日报》摘录的文章，鉴于东京方面的否认，该文读来颇有趣味。
《日本日报》的标题引述如下：
“孙科逃脱。我方海军飞机突袭客机。”
摘录内容指出，除其他事项外，“预计孙科先生将于早晨乘坐中国航空公司飞机离开香港，而在其离开香港后不久，我方海军飞机追逐该中航飞机，意图将其包围。
‘我们的猛鹰’意图活捉孙科先生。”
摘录接着列举了后续发展，这些情况目前已广为人知。

TRANSLATION
The radiogram "160025" has come to hand. In accordance
with your instructions, the Tai Woo Insurance Company was
immediately notified of the matter. However, during a
previous interview with Mr. Parson of the Company, he stated
that any untoward incident involving staff employees and
passengers of the Passage Liner "Kweiling," or damage done
to the machine as the result of its being attacked, is beyond
the usual sphere of insurance on the ground that such case
arises out of accident. Unless it is insured against war
risk, there is no likelihood that the company would grant
compensation.
As we have now decided to reserve all rights for
demanding payment of compensation, I respectfully suggest
that a radiogram be despatched immediately to the Company
giving all details in English and that strong representations
made direct with the concern in question.
pages.zh:
译文
电报“160025”已收悉。遵照阁下指示，已立即通知泰和保险公司此事。然而，在此前与该公司帕森（Parson）先生的面谈中，他表示，任何涉及“桂林”号客轮船员和乘客的不幸事件，或因飞机遭受攻击而造成的损坏，均超出通常的保险范围，理由是此类案件属于意外事故。除非投保了战争险，否则公司不太可能给予赔偿。
鉴于我方现已决定保留要求支付赔偿的一切权利，谨建议立即向该公司发送一份详细列明所有细节的英文电报，并向有关公司提出强烈交涉。

Date August 26, 1938.
Subject CNAC Aeroplane No. 32, "Kweilin" - Forced Down and Machine-
gunned by Japanese pursuit craft near Canton on August 24.
Made by D/S. Pitts. Forwarded by
In regard to the forcing down and subsequent machine-
gunning of a CNAC 'plane by Japanese pursuit craft in the
vicinity of Canton on August 24, 1938, I forward herewith
cablegrams sent and received by the local representative of
the CNAC, in respect to this tragedy. Enclosure (1)
clearly states that the damaged plane is completely under
the water and that twelve passengers, one co-pilot and
the steward - fourteen persons in all - are missing.
According to enclosure (2) the plane was forced
down at Changkibien in the Chungshan district of Canton
at 8.38 a.m. August 24 whilst flying from Hongkong on a
northbound trip.
Further details are at present unavailable from the
local representative.
D. S.
D.C. (Special Branch).

报告
日期：1938年8月26日。
事由：中国航空公司32号飞机，“桂林”号——8月24日在广州附近被日本追击机强迫降落并遭机枪扫射。
制作人：侦探警佐 Pitts。转呈人：
关于1938年8月24日中国航空公司一架飞机在广州附近被日本追击机强迫降落并随后遭机枪扫射一事，现随函附上中国航空公司当地代表就此悲剧发出和收到的电报。附件（1）明确指出，受损飞机已完全沉入水中，十二名乘客、一名副驾驶和一名服务员——共十四人——下落不明。
根据附件（2），该飞机于8月24日上午8时38分在从香港北上的飞行途中，被迫降落在广州中山县的张溪边（Changkibien）。
目前当地代表处暂无更多详情。

pages.en:
TRANSLATION

The radiogram "124024" has been noted, and
the Insurance Company has been informed of the matter.
This Company states that as it arises out of an
accident, the matter is beyond the sphere of insurance.

Local foreign and Chinese newspapers of to-day's
issue, however, published stories with conspicuous
headings on the subject, stating that over ten persons
in the Passage Liner "Kweiling" were killed, only a
Mr. Lur among the passengers, Pilot Mr. Woods and
another Loo Tsao-ming, altogether three persons,
escaping. Please immediately notify us by radiogram
all details.
pages.zh:
译文

电报“124024”已阅悉，并已通知保险公司此事。
该公司表示，由于此事属于意外事故，故不在保险范围之内。

然而，今日发行的本地中外报纸均以显著标题刊登了相关报道，称“桂林”号客轮上有十余人遇难，乘客中仅有一名卢（Lur）先生、飞行员伍兹（Woods）先生以及另一名罗肇明（Loo Tsao-ming），共计三人逃生。请立即用电报通知我们所有详情。

pages.en:
August 25, 1938.
Afternoon Translation.

Ta Mei Pao (Canton telegram) and other local newspapers :-

C.N.A.C. PLANE ATTACKED BY JAPANESE AEROPLANES

At 9 a.m. August 24, when the plane "Kweilin"
(桂林) of the China National Aviation Corporation, a
Sino-American concern, carrying 13 passengers and piloted
by an American named Woods, was on its way from Hongkong
to Chungking, Szechuen Province, it was attacked by five
Japanese aeroplanes over the sea near Canton. The plane
was struck by many bullets and made a forced landing in
the sea. After dropping several bombs, the Japanese
planes left.
The American pilot, a radio operator and a
wounded passenger named Ler (梅) were saved, but all the
other passengers were wounded and perished in the sea.
Two of the survivors have reached the city of Chung San (中山)
and entered a hospital for treatment.
Planes of the China National Aviation
Corporation have very clear distinguishing marks and all
foreign nations were notified. The atrocious attack
will probably draw a protest from America and the world.
Efforts are being made to salvage the plane
and the remains of the lost passengers.

Information secured from a certain large
Chinese bank in Shanghai shows that Mr. Sun Fo, President
of the Legislative Yuan of the National Government, had
originally intended to travel by this plane, but later he
took another plane. Mr. Singloh Hsu (徐新六), General
Manager of the National Commercial Bank, Shanghai, and a
member of the S.M.C., and Mr. Hu Pei-kong (胡筆江), Manager
of the Bank of Communications, Shanghai, were on the ill-
fated plane and their fate is unknown.
Mr. Singloh Hsu, age 49, native of Chekiang,
is a graduate of Birmingham University, England, and of
Victoria University, Manchester. After teaching in
Peking University, he became a secretary of the Ministry
of Finance of the National Government and a member of the
Chinese Delegation to the Paris Peace Conference. At
present, Mr. Hsu is General Manager of the National
Commercial Bank and a Director of the Tai San (泰山)
Insurance Company, the China Steel Company, the China
Development Finance Corporation, the Sz Hai (四海) Insurance
Company, the "China Press", the Bank of Communications,
the China Development Bank, the Chapei Water and Electricity
Company and of many other concerns in Shanghai. He is
one of the Chinese members of the S.M.C.
Mr. Hu Pei-kong, age 58, a native of Kiangsu,
is Manager of the Bank of Communications, Managing-Director
of the China & South Sea Bank, Director of the Bank of
China, the China Development Finance Corporation, the
China State Bank, and other banks. He is a member of the
Finance Advisory Committee of the National Government.
Mrs. Singloh Hsu, living in Great
Western Road became very anxious upon learning of the
disaster which befell the plane "Kweilin". She at once
sent a telegram to Canton and Hankow to enquire about her
husband, but up to 1 a.m. August 25, no reply had been
received.

1938年8月25日。
下午译件。

《大美报》（广州电）及其他本地报纸：

中国航空公司飞机遭日本飞机袭击

8月24日上午9时，中美合资企业中国航空公司（C.N.A.C.）的“桂林”号飞机，载有13名乘客，由一名名叫伍兹（Woods）的美国飞行员驾驶，从香港飞往四川省重庆途中，在广州附近海域上空遭到五架日本飞机的袭击。该机被多发子弹击中，被迫在海面降落。日军飞机投下数枚炸弹后离去。
美国飞行员、一名无线电操作员以及一名名叫勒（Ler，梅）的受伤乘客获救，但其余所有乘客均受伤并溺亡于海中。两名幸存者已抵达中山（Chung San）市，并入院接受治疗。
中国航空公司的飞机具有非常清晰的识别标志，且已通知所有外国政府。这一暴行可能会引起美国及全世界的抗议。
目前正努力打捞飞机及遇难乘客的遗体。

从上海某家大型中国银行获得的消息显示，国民政府立法院院长孙科先生原计划乘坐此航班，但后来改乘另一架飞机。上海浙江兴业银行总经理、工部局董事徐新六（Singloh Hsu）先生，以及上海交通银行经理胡笔江（Hu Pei-kong）先生均在上述失事飞机上，其命运尚不清楚。
徐新六先生，49岁，浙江人，毕业于英国伯明翰大学及曼彻斯特维多利亚大学。在北京大学任教后，他出任国民政府财政部秘书，并担任中国出席巴黎和会代表团成员。目前，徐先生任浙江兴业银行总经理，并担任泰山（Tai San）保险公司、中国钢铁公司、中国建设银公司、四海（Sz Hai）保险公司、《字林西报》（China Press）、交通银行、中国开发银行、闸北水电公司以及上海许多其他企业的董事。他是工部局华董之一。
胡笔江先生，58岁，江苏人，任交通银行经理，中南银行常务董事，中国银行、中国建设银公司、中国国家银行（China State Bank）及其他银行的董事。他是国民政府财政咨询委员会委员。
居住在大西路（Great Western Road）的徐新六夫人得知“桂林”号飞机遭遇灾难后，十分焦急。她立即向广州和汉口发电报询问丈夫情况，但截至8月25日凌晨1时，尚未收到回复。
